question: Should exact requester consumption count as terminal delivery proof for a descendant, suppressing later descendant retry even if the requester's final outward send fails?
rationale: Tests can prove the implementation matches either policy, but they cannot choose whether internal requester consumption or externally visible descendant delivery is the product's terminal delivery boundary.

options.title: Accept requester consumption after proof
options.body: Treat exact matched requester consumption as delivered after a current-main rebase and real cron/restart proof confirms only consumed descendants lose retry eligibility.

options.title: Require visible descendant delivery
options.body: Keep descendant rows retryable until their own visible delivery succeeds, even when requester orchestration has already consumed their output.

options.title: Fold into durable inbox design
options.body: Pause this patch and define requester consumption within the broader durable completion inbox or spool contract tracked by related delivery-loss work.

recommendation.title: Accept requester consumption after proof
recommendation.body: Treat exact matched requester consumption as delivered after a current-main rebase and real cron/restart proof confirms only consumed descendants lose retry eligibility.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history places the current cron delivery and persistent registry integration surfaces in their area, making them the best available routing candidate for the delivery-boundary decision.
